statement: The historical J-curve (light-to-moderate drinking 'protective' for all-cause/CV mortality) is largely an artifact of abstainer/sick-quitter bias and healthy-user confounding; the protective signal does not survive bias correction.
effect_size: Bias-corrected meta of 107 cohorts (~4.8M people): no significant mortality reduction for low-volume drinkers

provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-9 exposures brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: The refutation is of the PROTECTIVE claim, not of all structure. Reference-group bias is the core mechanism. Pair with Biddinger 2022 MR.

statement: Mendelian randomization using genetic instruments shows alcohol's relationship to cardiovascular disease is monotonic and steepening, not J-shaped; the apparent light-drinking benefit reflects confounding by favorable lifestyle traits.
effect_size: Genetically-predicted higher intake -> substantially higher CVD risk; risk accelerates at higher intake; no protective dip

provenance.primary: Biddinger KJ, Emdin CA, Haas ME et al. - 'Association of Habitual Alcohol Intake With Risk of Cardiovascular Disease', JAMA Network Open 2022
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-9 exposures brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: MR graded at rct-tier proxy: genotype is randomized at conception, breaking reverse causation. Strongest single design on this question. Not a literal RCT.

statement: Summed across all health outcomes, the level of alcohol consumption that minimizes total health loss is zero; the small cardiovascular offset is overwhelmed by cancer and injury.
effect_size: GBD 2016: minimum-risk consumption level = 0 standard drinks/week when all outcomes summed

provenance.primary: GBD 2016 Alcohol Collaborators (Griswold MG et al.) - 'Alcohol use and burden for 195 countries and territories, 1990-2016', The Lancet 2018

statement: The theoretical minimum-risk level of alcohol is age-dependent: effectively zero for younger adults (injury-dominated harm), and near one standard drink/day for older adults where the modest CV/diabetes offset is more relevant.
effect_size: TMREL ~0 drinks/day for adults <40; ~1 drink/day near risk minimum for older adults

provenance.primary: GBD 2020 Alcohol Collaborators (Bryazka D, Reitsma MB, Griswold M et al.) - 'Population-level risks of alcohol consumption by amount, geography, age, sex, and year', The Lancet 2022

statement: All-cause mortality risk is lowest at roughly <=100 g pure alcohol/week (~5-6 standard drinks) and rises approximately monotonically above that; alcohol lowers non-fatal MI but raises stroke, fatal aneurysm, heart failure and fatal hypertensive disease.
effect_size: Risk minimum ~100 g/week; condition-specific divergence (MI down, stroke/aneurysm/HF up)

statement: (SUPERSEDED VIEW) Moderate alcohol intake is associated with lower cardiovascular mortality vs abstainers and heavy drinkers (the J-curve).

statement: Lifelong cigarette smoking shortens life expectancy by approximately 10 years versus never-smoking; current smokers have roughly 3x all-cause mortality and up to two-thirds of their deaths are attributable to smoking.
effect_size: ~10 years of life lost; all-cause mortality RR ~2.5-3x; ~2/3 of smoker deaths attributable
population: British male doctors (50 yr); US NHIS (Jha); 204,953 Australians (Banks)

statement: Smoking cessation before age 40 avoids about 90% of the excess mortality from continued smoking; cessation at 30/40/50/60 recovers roughly 10/9/6/3 years of life.

statement: E-cigarettes help adult smokers quit (moderate-certainty, more effective than nicotine-replacement therapy) and eliminate combustion products, but are not safe in absolute terms and the population-level cost is nicotine initiation in never-smoking youth.

statement: Personal PM2.5 dose is reducible: indoor HEPA filtration cuts indoor particulate concentrations, AQI-aware behavior limits peak exposure, and avoiding high-traffic exercise prevents exertion-multiplied inhaled dose.
